title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to AI transcription at a urologist appointment, but the tool invented that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She found the false claim in a post-surgery letter to her GP after kidney stone surgery in March, and feared it could harm her workers' compensation case. After she complained, the urologist apologized, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A Digital Rights Watch report found similar errors, such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis, and estimated 40 per cent of GPs regularly use AI scribes. Australia's drug and medical device regulator, the TGA, says no AI scribes are approved and its review findings will be released in the coming weeks, with breaches acted upon. The advocacy group wants an AI Safety Institute to test and publish approved tools. Ms Green says she would only consent again with a doctor she already knows.
